condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

? Project launch event, inception workshop, ten Operation Coordination Unit meetings and two Project Steering Committee Meetings were held. Additionally an on the Spot Check Monitoring Meeting was organized by the Contracting Authority on 30 June 2020. ? Recruitment processes of the Project Team were finalized. ? Procurement processes were completed for the key experts on climate impacts and modeling, sectoral adaptation, and urban adaptation (on 3 June 2020, 15 July 2020, and 25 June 2020 respectively). The key expert on software development and database management, who was contracted under POPS project, also became eligible to assist CCA team after an amendment was made to the ICs contract. ? The Inception Report and all the annexes with Turkish translation were officially submitted on 12 May 2020 and officially approved on 4 June 2020. ? The First Activity Report and all the annexes with Turkish translation were officially submitted on 12 August 2020 and officially approved on 18 September 2020. ? English and Turkish Versions of the Second Activity Report were approved and will be officially submitted after the official submission letter is signed. ? The First Progress Report was submitted for approval on 07.12.2020. ? Four pilot metropolitan municipalities (Konya, Mugla, Sakarya, Samsun) were identified based on a prioritization study in collaboration with the stakeholders. ? Consultative meetings on urban adaptation guidelines and city typologies, software development of national adaptation platform and climate change impact assessments were held (via Zoom platform as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic). ? Grant guidelines were submitted and approved. Multiple Info-day/training sessions on the CCAGP were held with the relevant stakeholders (via Zoom platform as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic). ? Consultative meetings on city level impact and vulnerability assessments with the representative of pilot metropolitan municipalities will be held during the course of December 2020. As of 23 December 2020, the first three of these meetings were completed successfully. ? Reports on the assessment of the climate models used by the Turkish State Meteorological Services and DG Water Management , on existing climate change adaptation works / guidelines, on existing climate change adaptation grant programmes, on national adaptation platforms and EU Climate Adaptation Platform (Climate-ADAPT), and on monitoring and evaluation systems at national and local level (for the NASAP and UASAPs) were submitted. ? Activities related with the capacity building component have been initiated and two draft working documents for the main report have been submitted. Due to the pandemic, trainings, seminars, events and relevant desk studies have been postponed. ? The design process of the National Adaptation Platform including technical background and user interface has been initiated. The initial design will be ready by April 2021.

Component 1
• Regarding comprehensive climate change impact and vulnerability assessment for five priority sectors, preparing a climate vulnerability assessment, estimating of economic impacts of climate change and cost of adaptation measures for priority sectors with a baseline “business as usual” scenario for comparison and a preparing final report including findings and meeting proceedings.
• Regarding the adaptation options for updating the NASAP, compiling sectoral adaptation strategies for the priority sectors including structural and non-structural adaptation measures and using the vulnerability index map developed in Activity 1.2. Thereafter, conducting 5 one-day consultative meetings to discuss and identify adaptation measures for each priority sector. Study is expected to be completed with compilation of a final report including findings and meeting proceedings.
• Regarding the updated NASAP through multi-stakeholder process, preparing a plan for the NASAP update process, disseminating reports elaborated under activities 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3 among key stakeholders to identify priority adaptation activities. Organizing 10 1-day & 3 2-day consultative meetings for the prioritization of adaptation activities, finalizing the update of the NASAP which will include: (i) strategic priorities and areas of intervention in accordance of SDGs, (ii) an action plan with a list of selected climate change adaptation solutions, (iii) capacity building activities of relevant stakeholders, and (iv) a coordination mechanism among national entities (public, private, academia, civil society) at different levels and with international organizations. The updated NASAP will then be submitted to the higher authorities of the MoEU for its endorsement through the legislative body. The work will be disseminated among central and local authorities, civil society, academia, the private sector and the international community.
• Regarding the M&E, communication and the reporting system for the NASAP, setting up an online M&E system for that encompasses the identified set of indicators and will require all involved stakeholders to report into, preparing a training module on the use of these systems systems, and organizing 4 two-days training sessions to relevant stakeholders from public, private, academia and civil society.
• Regarding the climate financing strategy for the NASAP, conducting a desk review take stock of existing and expected future climate financing mechanisms at international and national level, to analyze climate financing strategies of selected EU member states with national adaptation strategies and to evaluate existing finance mechanisms for other themes for best practices and lessons learned. Organizing 5 one-day consultative meetings to discuss existing and expected future financial models, mechanisms and priorities for climate financing. Establishing a financing framework, a climate finance action plan and a final climate finance strategy.
• Regarding the adaptation plan implementation guidelines for 5 priority sectors, conducting a desk review to take stock of existing sector specific guidelines among EU member states and countries with similar socio-economic profiles, and to evaluate ongoing reforms and implementation mechanisms (i.e. policy making and project lifecycle) within the priority sectors. Organizing 5 one-day consultative meetings to identify institutional and technical needs for adaptation to be implemented successfully.
Component 2
• Regarding the climate change impact and vulnerability assessment for 4 pilot metropolitan municipalities, estimating the financial needs of adaptation for each city and potential market for adaptation at national scale, with a baseline “business as usual” scenario for comparison. Thereafter, preparing a final report including findings and meeting proceedings.
• Regarding the preparation of UASAPs for 4 pilot metropolitan municipalities, compiling / updating 4 UASAPs, organizing 4 two-day consultative meetings to discuss prioritization of action plans in cities and a media launch in Ankara for 200 people about each city and dissemination materials in different formats for different target audiences/stakeholders.
• Regarding the M&E system for the UASAP, organizing 4 one-day consultative meetings to discuss the M&E system layout at city level, setting up an online M&E system for cities that encompasses the identified set of indicators and will require all involved stakeholders to report into, preparing a training module on the use of M&E systems and organizing 4 two-days training sessions. Reviewing the priorities and activities identified in the UASAPs to assess progress, effectiveness and gaps. Conducting outreach of the UASAPs and the progress reports at national level through national communications and various media tools.
• Regarding the urban climate financing strategy, conducting a desk review to take stock of existing climate financing mechanisms at city level among EU member states, to analyze climate financing strategies of selected EU member states with UASAPs, and to evaluate existing finance mechanisms in Turkish cities for other themes for best practices and lessons learned. Assessing different financial solutions and later organizing a conference bringing IFIs and local authorities together to explore IFIs’ global experience in urban climate financing, and discuss suitable solutions for Turkish cities. Thereafter, preparing an urban climate financing strategy for the implementation of the UASAPs, a training module on the financial mechanisms and 4 two-days training sessions.
Component 3
• For capacity building and networking, preparing at least 10 customized climate change adaptation training modules and starting the work on the organization of these trainings. Conducting additional consultative meetings with the participation of the relevant public, private, academic and civil society stakeholders to present their experience with different city networks and advise on membership.
• For the establishment of the National Adaptation Platform, organizing the media launch and technical presentation of the platform to key stakeholders; Media launch will be in Ankara with participation of 200 people.
• Preparation and conduction of training modules covering “Grant Scheme Implementation Process” including guidelines development, launch, evaluation and contracting; and “Grant Projects Management and Monitoring” including implementation rules, contract management and monitoring and evaluation.
• Preparation and conduction of Information Days for applicants who are eligible to submit a full application.
• Technical assistance and administrative assistance during grant implementation and review, including monitoring visits under Climate Change Adaptation Grant Programme (CCGAP).
• Setting up a web-based grant management information system (MIS) for grantees to follow up their notification/amendment requests for grant projects, share project deliverables, reporting inputs for M&E, and visibility. The system will also be used for conducting interim and final evaluations of grant projects by MOEU/DGEUFR.
• Organizing the opening event of the grant programme.
• Establishing an M&E system including: (i) definition of metrics for documenting progress, measuring and communicating levels of effectiveness, (ii) an online M&E system for the Contracting Authority that encompasses the identified set of indicators in grant projects and will require all involved stakeholders to report into and (iii) regular reviews of activities undertaken as part of the grant.
• Organizing one consultative meeting throughout the course of the grant program to exchange information, assess progress and encourage collaboration among grant nominees.

Component 1
Regarding comprehensive climate change impact and vulnerability assessment for priority sectors, • Sector specific vulnerability assessment was submitted on 11 April 2022. The comments and reviews were received. The report is currently under revision. • The draft Climate Change Economy Report was submitted to the End Recipient. The submission date of the final report was 8 November 2022. • The draft final report including findings and meeting proceedings will be submitted to the End Recipient on 12 December 2022.
Regarding the adaptation options for updating the NASAP, • Consultative meetings to identify adaptation options as a long list by stakeholders was held between 18-22 April 2022 in Ankara. Draft meeting report was submitted for review on 24 August 2022 and approved on 6 September 2022. (EV4) • A final report including findings and meeting proceedings was submitted for review on 26 September 2022
Regarding the updated NASAP through multi-stakeholder process, • 10 one-day consultative meetings were held between 19-30 September 2022 and 3 two-day consultative meetings will be held between 7-9 and 13-15 December 2022 for the prioritization of adaptation activities. Meeting report of the first session was submitted on 7 December 2022. Both events were held in Ankara. • The updated NASAP will then be submitted to the higher authorities of the MoEU for its endorsement through the legislative body following the completion and the discussions in the meetings. The work will be disseminated among central and local authorities, civil society, academia, the private sector and the international community.
Regarding the climate financing strategy for the NASAP, • A desk review to take stock of existing and expected future climate financing mechanisms at international and national level, (ii) to analyze climate financing strategies of selected EU member states with national adaptation strategies, and (iii) to evaluate existing finance mechanisms for other themes for best practices and lessons learned was conducted. Draft report was submitted on 8 February 2022. The comments from ER were received on 27 May 2022. The revised document was submitted on 27 July 2022. • Consultative meetings to discuss existing and expected future financial models and mechanisms and priorities for climate financing were held between 10-14 October 2022 in Ankara. Draft meeting report was submitted on 6 December 2022.
Component 2
Regarding the climate change impact and vulnerability assessment for 4 pilot metropolitan municipalities, • 4 urban climate impact and vulnerability assessment draft reports were submitted for four pilot cities (Submission dates: 08.12.2021 Konya, 22.12.2021 Samsun, 11.01.2022 Mugla, 28.01.2022 Sakarya) and are under revision in line with the comments. • A draft final report on climate impact and vulnerability assessments including findings and meeting proceedings was submitted on 8 February 2022.
Regarding the preparation of UASAPs for 4 pilot metropolitan municipalities, • Additional consultative meetings on prioritization of local climate change actions were organized in Samsun on 14-15 June 2022, in Konya on 16-17 May 2022, in Sakarya on 30-31 May 2022, in Mugla on 22-23 June 2022 upon discussion during the project’s 17th OCU meeting held on 4 August 2021. • The urban adaptation strategy and action plans for Konya and Mugla were submitted on 10 October 2022. Action plans for Samsun and Sakarya are currently being reviewed by PT and will be submitted soon.
Regarding the urban climate financing strategy, • A desk review to take stock existing climate financing mechanisms at city level among EU member states, (ii) to analyze climate financing strategies of selected EU member states with UASAPs, and (iii) to evaluate existing finance mechanisms in Turkish cities for other themes for best practices and lessons learned was conducted. The draft working paper was submitted on 8 February 2022. The comments from ER were received on 27 May 2022. The revised document was submitted on 27 July 2022.
Component 3
For capacity building and networking, a study visit was held in Valladolid and Madrid, Spain between 28 November and 2 December 2022. Software development of the National Adaptation Platform (Climate Portal) was completed and currently content upload is being done by the MEUCC.
Regarding CCAGP,
• Last sessions of ‘Grant Scheme Implementation Process’ Training were held on 25 April 2022. ‘Grant Projects Management and Monitoring’ Training were held in premises of MoEUCC on 12 and 13 September. • Information days for the candidates who are eligible to submit a full application were organized on 22 and 23 March 2022 through online tools. • Draft MIS was developed for trial and testing purposes at the https://mis.iklimeuyum.org/ website address and shared with the CA.

The studies in the second year of the project provided a strong basis for the development of policy, technical and operational baselines to establish an enabling environment for climate change adaptation in Turkey.
Under Component 1
• The report on existing climate change adaptation works including the comparative assessment, multi-parameter analysis framework, classification system, compilation of existing work and list of best practices was submitted to and approved by the End Recipient • Sensitivity analysis to understand the performance of the climate models was submitted to and approved by the End Recipient • Climate projections update for sector use using Global Circulation Models outputs with regional models and available Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change scenarios was submitted to and approved by the End Recipient • An indicator-based climate vulnerability assessment scoping including a synopsis of the sectors, key stakeholders, and a methodology for a vulnerability index map in line with IPCC (AR5) was submitted to and approved by the End Recipient • The consultative meetings were held on water resources, agriculture, tourism / cultural heritage social development, health, industry, urban, transportation / communication, energy, ecosystem services (land, coast) sectors. It was organized online with the participation of public institutions, universities, non-governmental organizations and private sector representatives. In the meetings, sectoral vulnerability and risk analysis methodology was consulted within the framework of climate hazards, exposure, sensitivity, adaptation capacity factors. The meeting report summarizing the discussion and incorporating the contributions from the stakeholder representatives was submitted to and approved by the End Recipient • The studies for 10 sector climate vulnerability assessment covering a brief sector overview with trends, volume, affinities, opportunities, threats and uncertainties, the main vulnerability factors to different climatic hazards, existing adaptive capacity, and annualized impact estimation, including any potential domino impact (within the same sector) and cascading impact (to other sectors) have been initiated. • The Climate Change Economy Report was submitted to and approved by the End Recipient . • A desk review of NASAP prioritization methodologies among EU member states, including good practices and lessons learned and a stock-taking exercise on national strategies and policies for priority sectors, and international commitments and developments under multilateral environmental processes, such as the Paris Agreement, Sendai Framework and SDGs was submitted to and approved by the End Recipient • A comparative analysis of the Turkish NASAP with selected EU member states, including the elaboration and update process, organizational and financial aspects, methodologies used for developing the strategy and prioritizing the actions, and recommendations for improvement in the context of Turkey with linkages to the SDGs was submitted to and approved by the End Recipient. Additionally, a two-day consultative meeting on the updating methodology of NASAP was organized where presentations on the examples from EU countries on climate change strategy and action plan preparations, multiple hazard assessments results for Turkey, current national climate change adaptation strategy and action plan (2011-2023) preparation process, methodologies for prioritizing actions, and the EU country examples were made. The discussions were made with the stakeholder representatives from academia, public institutions, private sector, NGOs and local government • A desk review to take stock of existing adaptation indicators and governance mechanisms from EU member states, identify relevant indicators already existing in national and local M&E systems, and identify different M&E governance models (e.g. climate M&E officer, assigned staff under climate change unit) applicable for Turkey and staff time, budget and capacity development required for these models was submitted to and approved by the End Recipient.
Under Component 2
• Adaptation guidelines and urban typology framework for cities was submitted to and approved by the End Recipient • A review and update of climate projections for urban use using Global Circulation Models outputs with regional models and available Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change scenarios was submitted to and approved by the End Recipient • An urban climate vulnerability assessment scoping including a synopsis of the 4 pilot cities with socio-economic, environmental and organizational overview, key stakeholders, and a methodology for an urban vulnerability index map which accounts for the vulnerabilities of regional economic linkages and ecosystems that make up the hinterland of urban areas was submitted to and approved by the End Recipient • The report based on the meetings held on December 2020 to discuss the “Climate Change Impact and Vulnerability Assessment in Four Pilot Cities was submitted and approved” • In addition, 4 two-day hybrid consultative meetings were held on 6-7 July 2021 for Sakarya, 12-13 July 2021 for Konya, 19-20 August 2021 for Samsun and 23-24 July 2021 for Mugla with the participation of the representatives from the stakeholders from the public sector, private sector, civil society, and academia. Following the presentations made by the project experts, the issues on data provision for the vulnerability and risk assessments, and challenges and opportunities faced by the cities in the adaptation processes to climate change were consulted. • The studies for 4 urban climate impact and vulnerability assessment covering a brief sector overview with trends, volume, affinities, opportunities, threats and uncertainties, the main vulnerability factors to different climatic hazards, the existing adaptive capacity, and the annualized impact estimation, including any potential domino impact (within the same sector) and cascading impact (to other sectors) have been initiated. • A desk review of city-wide adaptation actions based on vulnerability assessments through stakeholder engagement at EU level and within EU member states was submitted to and approved by the End Recipient • In order to develop adaptation plans to climate change at the local level, 4 one-day online consultative meetings were held on 7 June 2021 for Sakarya, 8 June 2021 for Konya, 9 June 2021 for Mugla and 10 June 2021 for Samsun with the participation of 262 representatives from the stakeholders from the public sector, private sector, civil society, and academia to discuss the local climate change adaptation strategy and action plans • During the meetings scheduled for a full day, following the presentation of the climate change adaptation strategy and action plan process to the stakeholders, presentations were made by the project experts on the issues of the sectoral impacts of climate change, action plans and adaptation actions. • The studies for 4 UASAPs for the pilot cities including structural and non-structural adaptation measures and using the vulnerability index map developed in Activity 2.2 has been initiated. • A desk review to take stock of existing adaptation indicators and governance mechanisms (e.g. SMART indicators) from EU cities, to identify relevant indicators already existing in national and local M&E systems, and to identify different M&E governance models (e.g. climate M&E officer, assigned staff under climate change unit) applicable for cities in Turkey and staff time, budget and capacity development required for these models was submitted to and approved by End Recipient
Under Component 3
• Consultative meetings were held via online tools for project stakeholders (public institutions, universities, non-governmental organizations and private sector) between 14-16 June 2021 and four pilot cities between 21-22 June 2021 with the participation of 552 representatives in total. Draft meeting report was submitted to End Recipient. • In the meetings, adaptation process was consulted within the framework of capacity building and basic assumptions for inclusive adaptive action, stakeholder needs and options, and general elements and implementation methods of the capacity building plan. • Policy and stakeholder capacity and need assessment was submitted to End Recipient • A capacity building plan was submitted to End Recipient • A desktop review and meetings with related stakeholders to take stock of similar national platforms among EU member states and at EU-level (such as climate-ADAPT), to provide recommendations for the national adaptation platform, to identify knowledge gaps and communication issues among Turkish stakeholders, and to identify international and national networks and online platforms and libraries of relevance and interest was submitted to and approved by End Recipient • Software design and test runs of the platform, including key components such as: FAQ, contact list, publication and activity database, search function, metadata download and report/map making services were completed • Content upload to the platform (publications, reports, media, etc.) and links with relevant networks and online platforms has been initiated. • Preparations for media launch and technical presentation of the platform to key stakeholders; presentation of climate change adaptation work per sector and development of sector specific infographics and presentation material; organization of two public events (i.e. contest, exhibition) on climate change adaptation work have been initiated. • The report based on the first two sessions of Grant Scheme Implementation Process Training held on December 2020 was submitted and approved. • Implementation Guidelines, Visibility Manual, Procurement Guidelines, Monitoring Guidelines together with their annexes were submitted and approved. Turkish translations of guidelines were submitted; first set of comments were received, and revised guidelines were re-submitted. • The report based on the first part of Information Days on concept note application process was held on October and November 2020 was submitted and approved. The draft agenda for second part of Information Days on full application process was submitted; comments were received, revised version was re-submitted.
